events.content:
Done — `/admin` now returns a real HTTP 403 with a styled error page for non-admins, verified end-to-end with the dev server.

What I added:

- **`app/admin/page.tsx`** — a server component that calls `verifyAdmin()` from your existing mock auth lib. If the session role isn't `admin`, it calls `forbidden()` from `next/navigation` (Next.js's built-in auth interrupt), which halts rendering and responds with a 403 status. Admins see the dashboard with their name.
- **`app/forbidden.tsx`** — the boundary that renders when `forbidden()` is thrown: a centered "403 — Forbidden" page explaining the area is admin-only, with a "Return home" link.
- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `experimental.authInterrupts: true`, which is still required for `forbidden()`/`forbidden.tsx` in this Next version (16.3 canary).

Verification: with the mock session's `user` role, `curl /admin` returned **HTTP 403** and the forbidden page body. I then temporarily flipped the mock role to `admin` and got **HTTP 200** with the "Admin Dashboard" content, then restored the mock back to `user` and stopped the dev server.

One note: since `app/forbidden.tsx` sits at the root, it will serve as the 403 boundary for any future `forbidden()` call app-wide. If you later want a different look for other sections, you can add segment-level `forbidden.tsx` files. There's also a matching `unauthorized()` / `unauthorized.tsx` pair for 401s if you need to distinguish "not logged in" from "logged in but not allowed".
